question: When were the stars made?
summary: Genesis 1:16-19 has God making the stars on the fourth day of creation, after the earth already existed. Job 38:4-7 pictures the 'morning stars' already singing together when God laid the earth's foundations, placing the stars before the earth.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read Job's 'morning stars' as the angelic host present at the founding of the earth, a poetic figure, not the literal luminaries Genesis assigns to the fourth day.

discrepancy.connective: Thomas Paine objects that Genesis sets the luminaries in an order he finds impossible, faulting an account that times days and lights before the bodies that should produce them.

skeptic.name: Thomas Paine
skeptic.attribution: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason (1794)

pd_work.note: Clarke keys the harmonization to this passage, reading Job's 'morning stars' as the angelic host included under the 'heavens' of Genesis 1:1 rather than the literal stars of the fourth day.

link.title: How could there be light on the first day of Creation if the sun was not created until the fourth day?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of the day-one/day-four luminary ordering that underlies the stars-timing question.

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: This must refer to some intelligent beings who existed before the creation of the visible heavens and earth: and it is supposed that this and the following clause refer to the same beings; that by the sons of God, and the morning stars, the angelic host is meant… Perhaps their creation may be included in the term heavens, Gen 1:1: “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.”
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the chronology: the 'morning stars' of Job 38:7 are not the literal stars made on day four but the angelic host created with the 'heavens' of Gen 1:1, so there is no conflict.
excerpts.source_note_text: When the morning stars sang together - This must refer to some intelligent beings who existed before the creation of the visible heavens and earth: and it is supposed that this and the following clause refer to the same beings; that by the sons of God, and the morning stars, the angelic host is meant; as they are supposed to be first, though perhaps not chief, in the order of creation. For the latter clause the Chaldee has, "All the troops of angels." Perhaps their creation may be included in the term heavens, Gen 1:1 : "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth." These witnessed the progress of the creation; and, when God had finished his work, celebrated his wisdom and power in the highest strains.
